bare.rule: Track hidden net salt level = salts added minus acids added. Salt increases it by 1, acid decreases it by 1. Heat does not change it, but each heat 'develops' the current color: net <= 0 gives clear, net = 1 gives green, net >= 2 gives purple. Later salt/acid without another heat does not change the visible color; a later heat redevelops the color from the net level at that time.

random answers.rule: Track pending salt (salt added since the last heat) and activated salt (salt converted by heat). Salt increments pending; heat moves all pending into activated and resets pending to 0; acid has no effect. Color: clear if activated=0; clear if activated=1 and pending=0; green if activated=1 and pending>0; purple if activated=2 and pending=0.

rounds.rule: Track net salt minus acid. Whenever heat is applied, set the colour from that net at the moment of heating: net >= 2 becomes purple, net = 1 becomes green, and net <= 0 becomes clear. Salt or acid added after the last heat does not change the colour until another heat; with no heat, it stays clear.

commitments.why: The heat occurs with net salt-minus-acid = 1, so it sets green; the later acid should not change the colour until another heat. If it came out clear, acid after heat would immediately override the heated colour, contradicting the rule.
At the heat, net salt-minus-acid is 2, so purple is fixed; acid afterward should not change it. If it came out clear or green, acid after a heat would override the stored colour.
The heat sees net salt-minus-acid = 1 and sets green; a later salt without another heat should not change it. If it were purple, later salt would alter the heated colour or final net would matter.
No heat occurs, so the initial clear should remain even though net salt is 3. If it were green or purple, colour could be set without heating.
The first heat sees net 0 and stays clear; after one salt, the second heat sees net 1 and sets green. If it came out clear or purple, the heat-time net rule or threshold would be wrong.

rounds.rule: Heat toggles the vial between cold and hot. Salt raises a hidden count only when the vial is cold and not blocked by acid; acid added cold resets the count and blocks salt, while acid added hot waits until the next cooling to reset/block. Colour is clear at count 0, green at 1, and purple at 2 or more.

commitments.why: If this came out green, acid added hot would either not activate on cooling or would not block a later cold salt, contradicting the delayed/blocking acid rule.
If this came out clear, multiple acids added while hot would act immediately or accumulate to act hot, contradicting that hot acid waits for cooling.
If this came out green or purple, cold acid would not both reset the salt count and prevent the following cold salt from counting.
If this came out green or purple, acid would not fully reset a two-salt count, or heat would restore the salt colour.
If this came out clear or green, heating twice would change the salt-count colour rather than only toggling temperature.

attack, rebuild fresh.final_rule: Track a hidden value starting at 0. Adding salt increases it by 1; adding acid decreases it by 1. Heat sets the visible colour based on the current value: <=0 clear, exactly 1 green, >=2 purple. Salt/acid alone do not change the colour until the next heat.

rounds.rule: Heating converts salt into an active base; the color is clear with 0 active base units, green with 1, and purple with 2 or more. Acid neutralizes one salt/base unit only when a heating step occurs, so acid added without later heat does nothing.

commitments.why: If this were green or purple, acid would not cancel salt when both are present before heating; my rule says one salt and one acid heated together leave zero active units.
If this were clear, one acid would cancel both salts; if purple, acid would be ignored; my rule says one acid cancels only one of the two heated salts.
If this were clear or green, a later heat would not activate both salts added after an earlier heat; my rule counts two heated salt units.
If this were green or clear, acid would neutralize active salt without being heated; my rule says acid needs a heating step to cancel.
If this were clear, salt added after a first heat would not be activated by a later heat; my rule leaves one active salt unit, hence green.

rounds.rule: Salt adds latent base. Heat converts all latent base into active base and lets each acid neutralize one active base. Colour is clear for 0 active base, green for 1, and purple for 2 or more.

commitments.why: If this came out clear instead, the colour would cycle modulo 3 rather than saturating at purple for two or more active base units.
If this came out green or clear, acid would neutralize active base immediately without needing a later heat, contradicting the delayed acid action.
If this came out green, a later heat would not activate salt added after an earlier heat; my rule says the second heat activates it.
If this came out clear or purple, one acid would cancel either two salts or none when heated; my rule says it cancels exactly one.
If this came out green, acid added before salt would fail to neutralize the salt during the heat; my rule says heat lets them cancel.
